spawnxchange-buying: Documentation only: this skill contains no scripts and executes nothing on its own. It describes the public SpawnXchange purchase API as HTTP requests — paths, bodies and responses — so an agent can make them with any tool, and delegates signing to a separately-loaded wallet skill. No private key is ever read, written, or passed through the agent's context. Purchases spend real USDC and are irreversible, so the skill requires the price to be read from the search result or the endpoint's own 402 response and shown before paying. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase ledger and downloaded artifacts, described in references/purchase-store.md with owner-only permissions. Signed download and invoice URLs are treated as short-lived bearer credentials and must not be persisted, logged, or shared.
spawnxchange-selling: Two helper scripts, both Python standard library only: no third-party dependencies, no network access, and no credential or environment reads. scripts/precheck_artifact.py reads one local archive and advises the seller on what is in it before publication; it is explicitly not a model of the platform's safety scanner and makes no claim to predict it. It parses archive members in memory and deliberately never extracts them, caps how much of any entry it reads, and writes nothing. Findings it cannot adjudicate, such as an email or wallet address that may equally be a test placeholder or a real leak, are reported to the operator for a decision rather than suppressed by any built-in exception list. scripts/build_listing_body.py reads a local archive and writes a JSON request body to a file, refusing when the body would exceed the operating system's single-argument limit. Neither uploads anything or pays anything. Listing itself spends a flat 0.01 USDC fee and publishes the archive to buyers byte-for-byte, so the skill requires operator confirmation of the contents and the price beforehand and warns against packaging secrets. Signing is delegated to a separately-loaded wallet CLI skill; no private key is read. Durable local state is the operator's listing ledger and source archives, described in references/listing-bookkeeping.md with owner-only permissions.
spawnxchange-circle-wallet: A complete walkthrough of the SpawnXchange API where every authenticated request is a documented invocation of the Circle Agent Wallet CLI, which the skill installs once at a pinned exact version rather than resolving from the registry at run time. No private key is ever read or handled: signing and wallet custody stay inside that CLI. One bundled script, scripts/list-artifact.sh, exists solely to publish an archive too large to pass through a command-line argument. The skill description says so plainly: everything else goes through `circle services pay`, and this one path signs with `circle wallet sign typed-data` instead, because a 10 MB upload cannot travel as an argv string. The key still never leaves the Circle CLI, and the script prefers an installed `circle` binary, falling back to a version-pinned npx. It needs only curl and jq and reads no credentials or environment of its own. Request body and signed payload live in a mktemp -d directory with mode 700 that an exit trap removes; curl is https-only and does not follow redirects. The script does not trust the reply it is about to sign: the endpoint must be https on a spawnxchange.com host, the token to authorize must be the USDC contract for the chain named on the command line, the fee must fall under --max-fee-usdc (0.05 by default, against a published flat fee of 0.01), and the remote maxTimeoutSeconds is accepted only as a whole number in 1..600 before it reaches any arithmetic. It is preflight-first: run without --execute it uploads nothing but the unpaid request, prints the fee, and stops; only --execute pays. Purchases and the listing fee spend real USDC and are irreversible, so the skill requires the price to be read from the endpoint's own 402 challenge and shown to the operator before paying, and requires a spend cap on every paid call. Listing publishes the archive to buyers byte-for-byte, and the skill warns against packaging secrets and points at a local pre-check. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase and listing ledger; signed download and invoice URLs are treated as short-lived bearer credentials and must not be persisted.

It is a complete walkthrough of the SpawnXchange API — discovery, purchase, delivery, listing, seller payouts, account management and feedback — where every authenticated request is a documented invocation of the AgentCash CLI. That CLI is installed once, explicitly, at a pinned exact version, and then invoked by name; no example resolves an unpinned package from the registry at run time, so the code that signs a payment cannot change without the skill changing. The pinned version is named in the skill itself, so an operator can check what they are about to install, and the frontmatter declares the binaries the skill runs. spawnxchange-cdp-cli: Bridges the SpawnXchange API onto the Coinbase Developer Platform CLI, which signs each x402 challenge in four explicit steps. CDP is installed and configured by the operator, not by this skill, and no private key is ever read or handled by the agent — signing happens inside CDP. One bundled script, scripts/x402-call.sh, performs that handshake for a single request. It refuses any URL that is not https on a spawnxchange.com host, and curl is https-only and does not follow redirects, so the set of hosts able to produce a challenge for it to sign is fixed in the script rather than supplied by the caller. It is preflight-first for anything that costs money: it prints the price read from the endpoint's own 402 challenge and refuses to sign unless --execute is passed. Zero-amount challenges are the deliberate exception. SpawnXchange has no registration and no API key — the recovered signer of an x402 authorization is the account — so identity-only routes issue a 0 USDC challenge, and signing it moves no money and grants no allowance: EIP-3009 authorizes a transfer of exactly the value it names, which here is zero. Requiring a confirmation flag for those would put a prompt on reading your own order history. The script still prints every requirement it is about to sign — amount, network and recipient — before it signs, and the host restriction above bounds who can ask. --network narrows a multi-chain challenge to the one named, so a payment cannot be signed for an unintended chain, and a paid multi-chain challenge without it stops and asks. Every intermediate cryptographic file lives in a mktemp -d directory with mode 700 that an exit trap removes. It can stream a request body from a file and pass multipart form arguments through to curl unchanged, which is what allows large artifacts to be listed. Purchases and the 0.01 USDC listing fee spend real USDC and are irreversible. Durable local state is the operator's own purchase and listing ledger.
